<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD's top-level scope contains only standard variable definitions and a source array. The `source` array references the package's own upstream GitHub repository (`https://github.com/Tieske/uuid/archive/refs/tags/$pkgver.tar.gz`), which is expected upstream behavior for an AUR package. There are no `eval`, `base64`, `curl`, or `wget` commands at the top level, nor any command substitutions that would execute untrusted code during sourcing. The `sha512sums` array contains a proper checksum (not `SKIP`), and the `_archive` variable is a simple string interpolation. No suspicious network requests, obfuscated code, or unexpected file operations appear at the top level. All top-level code is consistent with ordinary AUR packaging practices.
</details>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD is for the lua-uuid package family (lua51-uuid through lua54-uuid), a pure Lua UUID generator by Tieske. The file follows standard AUR packaging practices with no suspicious elements.

The source is downloaded via the `source` array from the project's own GitHub release tarball (https://github.com/Tieske/uuid/archive/refs/tags/1.0.0.tar.gz), which is the expected upstream location. A sha512sum is provided and is not set to SKIP. The build process consists solely of standard packaging operations: `cd`, `install`, `find`, and directory creation—all operating within `$pkgdir`. No network requests occur during `build()` or `package()`. No use of `curl`, `wget`, `eval`, `base64`, or other potentially dangerous commands appears anywhere in the file.

The `_package()` helper function is invoked once per Lua version (5.1 through 5.5), installing the LICENSE file, the main `uuid.lua` module, and any Lua files found in subdirectories of the `uuid/` source tree. Optional dependencies (`lua*-socket` for time-based seeding and `lua*-system` for RNG) are standard for this library. There is no evidence of code injection, data exfiltration, obfuscated commands, or any deviation from ordinary Lua package packaging.</details>
<evidence>
